title: Trapezoid: A Versatile Accelerator for Dense and Sparse Matrix Multiplications
problem: Existing matrix multiplication accelerators are optimized for specific sparsity ranges—dense, mildly sparse, or highly sparse—but cannot efficiently handle the full spectrum of sparsities encountered in neural networks, graph analytics, and scientific computing.
motivation: Matrix multiplication acceleration is critical for achieving high performance across diverse applications that process matrices with varying sparsity levels, from completely dense to highly sparse.
method: Trapezoid starts with a 2D spatial array—a grid of processing units physically arranged on the chip—and adds specialized hardware for handling sparse matrices. For mildly sparse matrices, it uses an inner-product-based dataflow (organizing computation as dot products) paired with a multi-fiber intersection unit (hardware that processes multiple sparse data streams in parallel). For highly sparse matrices, it switches to a Gustavson-based dataflow (an algorithm optimized for sparse matrix multiplication) with a multi-level memory hierarchy (different-speed memory layers close and far from the processing cores). Crucially, all these specialized dataflows reuse the same underlying hardware rather than requiring separate chips, keeping the total size manageable.
key_novelty: Rather than building separate accelerators for dense, mildly sparse, and highly sparse matrices, Trapezoid is a single chip that efficiently handles all sparsity levels by switching between different computational patterns—all of which share the same underlying hardware.
contributions: 2D spatial array extended with sparse matrix handling hardware mechanisms
Inner-product-based dataflow with multi-fiber intersection unit for mildly sparse matrices
Gustavson-based dataflows with multi-level memory hierarchy for highly sparse matrices
Achieves 19.7x, 4.3x, and 2.9x better performance/area than TPU, SIGMA, and Flexagon respectively

metrics.speedup: 19.7x vs TPU, 4.3x vs SIGMA, 2.9x vs Flexagon
